elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted paragraph opens: "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, RevMed shall...", covering both expiry and every termination pathway rather than only the Change-of-Control mechanic in 12.3(e).

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: The operative insertion states "transition assistance for a period of at least ninety (90) days"; no six-month (or up to six months) duration appears in the rendered language. Six months is only mentioned in the margin comment, which is not operative.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: The inserted sentence contains no pricing basis at all; "at RevMed's then-current rates" (or equivalent) is absent from the operative text and appears only in the comment.

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "shall, within thirty (30) days after such expiration or termination, export and deliver to Sanofi all data belonging to, supplied by, or generated or processed for Sanofi" — the 30-day clock runs from expiry/termination, not from a request, and delivery (not just availability) is required.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: The insertion specifies no format; the words "commonly used, machine-readable format" do not appear anywhere in the rendered operative language.

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: No deletion-and-certification limb was added. Retained Section 11.6 only permits either Party to *request* destruction of Confidential Information at the non-requesting Party's election, with broad retention carve-outs and no fixed period — it is not a post-return certified deletion obligation owed by RevMed.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason" — the trigger is unconditional as to cause and covers both expiry and termination; the assistance period runs "following such expiration or termination", so it applies after every covered event, not merely in anticipation of expiry.

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: "at Sanofi's request, provide Sanofi with reasonable transition assistance for a period of at least ninety (90) days following such expiration or termination". The "at Sanofi's request" condition is a Customer election exercisable at any time, not a pre-expiry-only trigger, so the 90-day floor is intact.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "within thirty (30) days after such expiration or termination, export and deliver to Sanofi all data belonging to, supplied by, or generated or processed for Sanofi" — the export deadline is anchored to termination/expiry and the data scope covers every category belonging to, supplied by, or processed for the Customer.

reasons: The finding is correctly characterised as missing: Section 12.3(c)(vi) transition assistance runs from Sanofi to RevMed, Section 12.3(d) gives only a reverse licence, and Section 12.3(e) is confined to termination for a Change of Control involving a Major Biopharmaceutical Company with no stated duration and no data-export deadline. Section 11.6 is an election-based destruction-on-request provision for Confidential Information, not a Vendor-side return/export obligation.

All three fallback elements are met in operative language with the correct temporal anchors (assistance period and 30-day export both run from expiry/termination, not from a request), so the redline is position-complete at the fallback level.

Preferred is not reached: the insertion lacks the six-month duration, the then-current-rates pricing basis, the standard machine-readable format requirement, and the post-return certified-deletion limb. To reach preferred, the drafter must add in operative text: (a) "for up to six (6) months at RevMed's then-current rates"; (b) "in a commonly used, machine-readable format"; and (c) "thereafter delete all such data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing to Sanofi".

Minimality holds: the edit is a single concise inserted paragraph addressing only the three chosen fallback elements, with no survival tail, no at-own-expense or cost-allocation language, no added remedies or procedures, and no deletion or paraphrase of existing wording. Retained Sanofi-side obligations under 12.3(c)(vi) and the Section 11.6 retention carve-outs are untouched.

Intent is preserved: nothing is deleted, no defined term is orphaned, and no cross-reference dangles. The new export obligation coexists with Section 11.6, which is a Confidential Information destruction mechanic triggered only by a Party's written request. One drafting tidy-up worth making (not an element failure): give the inserted paragraph its section designation 12.3(f) as described in the rationale and confirm it is captured by the Section 12.4 survival list, so the export duty cannot be argued to lapse with the rest of Article XII.
